request: Where do the out-of-fold predictions for the stacking model come from?

composition.story: Stacking requires out-of-fold predictions to train the meta-model safely. Cross-validation splits training data into folds. Each base model predicts on left-out folds iteratively, ensuring unbiased features.

aha.observation: Out-of-fold predictions are generated by base models predicting exclusively on data they never saw during training.

states.label: Split Data
states.sentence: Divide training data into K distinct folds for cross-validation.
states.why: Prevents data leakage into the meta-learner.

states.label: Train Base Model
states.sentence: Train base estimators on K-1 folds, holding out one fold.
states.why: The holdout fold remains completely unseen.

states.label: Predict Out-of-Fold
states.sentence: Generate predictions on the held-out fold using the trained model.
states.why: These predictions form unbiased features for the meta-model.

states.label: Assemble Meta-Dataset
states.sentence: Concatenate all out-of-fold predictions to form the meta-training set.
states.why: The meta-model learns how to combine base predictions.
